registration: Fixed before performance runs. Implementation correctness tests may precede source freeze.
question: How much clearing potential can local cancellation and comfort-assisted headroom realise as communication increases, on static ledgers and with randomly timed transactions?
initial_balances: Uniform integer -6..6, with one canonical signed balance per undirected trustline.
topology: Connected ring plus uniformly drawn additional distinct undirected links; includes zero-balance trustlines.
comfort: Both endpoints opt in. Broad: shared zone equals hard interval [-10000,10000]. Narrow: independent symmetric endpoint widths from1,3,6; actual shared zone uses app comfort model.

arrivals.process: Poisson interarrival times, independent of algorithm RNG

service: Static: one fully drained call at total budget. Arrivals: message credits accrue linearly with time; before each offered arrival run fully drained clearing up to credits earned, then post arrival; one final bounded service call at end_time. Unused credits carry forward. No unbudgeted final search.
protocol: Reliable exactly-once, serialized research actors. Each actor uses own signed links/preferences and received direct-neighbour messages. Path-bearing tokens are allowed and disclosed. Complete search/prepare/commit/cleanup communication is counted; no crashes or concurrent arrivals during settlement.
headroom_rule: Every local incidence satisfies actual app comfort_move; neutral or exposure-increasing assistance requires both opt-ins. Initiator starts on a locally debt-reducing edge. Settle only cycles of at least3 nodes with strictly negative aggregate change in absolute balances. Helpers may increase within consented comfort, including zero links.
maximum_path: Number of nodes in the fixture, supplied as a fixed resource bound.
communication: Actual application-message attempts and compact JSON bytes, including search, rejection, preparation, commit and cleanup. x=actual messages/original undirected trustlines, counting zero links once. Excludes the externally injected transaction data, initial ledger/preferences distribution, network headers and ACKs absent from the reliable model.
reference: Replay accepted external transactions onto initial signed ledger WITHOUT clearing. All offered transactions must be accepted by every method, and this reference must remain within hard caps. The bound initial gross debt+sum absolute offered amounts<10000 proves this for strictly gross-reducing clearing.
oracle: Offline NetworkX3.5 min-cost flow: signed trustlines represented by two opposite capacity10000 cost1 arcs, fixed node net positions. Minimize gross debt=sum absolute signed balances. The oracle is never used by actors.
y: Clearing potential achieved (%)=100*(reference gross debt-actual gross debt)/(reference gross debt-oracle minimum gross debt). Preserve negative values; zero potential is undefined, not100%. This is final-snapshot savings, not cumulative historical settlement volume.
denominator_limits: Broad comfort admits the oracle's hard-bound state space. For narrow comfort this is a common relaxed ceiling; do not call it the exact preference-constrained reachable optimum. Unlike the original MDG2 cancellation-only benchmark, agreed headroom permits both balance directions on existing trustlines.
aggregation: Each panel compares three fixed graph/arrival seeds, with profiles sharing the same graphs and offers. Plot mean actual messages/trustline against ratio of summed savings to summed potential; show individual-seed traces. Do not count budget points or timing repetitions as independent graphs.
timing: One illustrative runtime sample per fixed case/policy/budget; communication, not latency, is the primary curve. Sequential runs; no performance tuning after inspection.
report: All results, including negative snapshot savings and preference limitations.
Offered/accepted/blocked transaction counts and value, remaining debt, discomfort, helper/restoration moves, actual messages, bytes and unused budget.
Independent replay of all settlements/transfers, per-node conservation, hard limits and comfort consent; independent oracle optimality check.
No claim of app protocol changes, production security, concurrency, fault tolerance or universal convergence from finite curves.
